A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same watermarking work. The main text, algorithms, results, figures, and Appendix A can be matched reliably; v2 adds Appendices B and C.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermarking experiments on Dolly and ELI5, including detection, text-quality, and attack results, plus simulations in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and simulations and adds example generated responses in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The sampling, deduplication, count-weighted selection, recursive watermarking, and detection procedures remain unchanged. Adding n to detector signatures makes an already-used input explicit; Appendix B supplies implementation code without establishing a revised method.

E1.justification: Dolly instruction-generation tasks, ELI5 questions, C4 reference data, and the corruption and paraphrasing scenarios are retained. The coffee-shop examples remain within existing task coverage. Appendix B's dummy-model demonstration provides code without reported simulation outcomes.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Aaronson, Aaronson Corrected, Kirchenbauer, Kuditipudi, and the decoding controls. Newly discussed SynthID and WATERMAX are not experimentally evaluated. Appendix C illustrates already evaluated methods.

E3.justification: The reported benchmark protocols retain 5,233 Dolly and 4,885 ELI5 examples, model settings, generation and truncation lengths, metrics, and attack procedures. The explicit n = 4 statement is newly disclosed information, not a reported setting revision.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a limited qualitative comparison of outputs for one coffee-shop prompt, showing four watermarking schemes and greedy decoding. Existing ablations, entropy analyses, detection studies, and robustness experiments remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 5.2 newly explains that standard errors come from repeated watermark generation with fixed secret keys. v1 already reported standard errors, and those values remain unchanged. The repetition count is still unspecified; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Appendix C adds concrete generated-text examples. Existing numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged across Tables 1-7 and Figures 1-7; for example, Table 1 still reports perplexity 2.61 and AUC 97.7% for flat watermarking with k = 1 and m = 1024.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.1-4.4, their assumptions, and the lemmas and proofs in Appendix A.3 retain their mathematical substance. Notational edits and expanded descriptions do not introduce new guarantees or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central claims: black-box watermarking, conditional distortion-free guarantees, recursive composition, white-box applicability, and competitive performance. The shortened introduction preserves these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 expands the limitations of measuring distortion through perplexity. It discusses KL divergence and its computational difficulty, and clarifies that fidelity concerns similarity to non-watermarked sampling rather than simply minimizing perplexity. Some result descriptions accordingly change 'better' perplexity to 'lower.'

D1.justification: New Appendix B substantially expands implementation information with Python code for flat and recursive generation and detection, hashing, deduplication, and a configured demonstration driver. v2 also explicitly specifies n = 4 and repairs omitted detector arguments in the pseudocode.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive comparisons with SynthID and WATERMAX, explaining encoding overlap and differences in detection, distortion guarantees, entropy analysis, and recursion. The acknowledgments newly credit earlier unpublished work whose flat k = 1 encoder is described as identical. These additions materially refine novelty and attribution; a Gemma reference is also added.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the introduction, expands selected related-work and evaluation passages, updates authorship and acknowledgments, and adds code and output-example appendices. Most existing prose and the principal section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves ahead of Table 1, and text reflows around retained displays. Appendices B and C introduce shaded, numbered code listings and monospaced output examples. Existing figure graphics, table structures, and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's already detailed pseudocode and results, v2 makes implementation more accessible through Appendix B, improves attribution to closely related work, and clarifies distortion measurement and standard-error estimation. These provide useful, bounded gains in reproducibility and interpretation. The existing scientific evidence is preserved, although experimental repetition counts remain unspecified.
